stops.note: 'book', first meaning the inner bark of a tree, an early writing surface; librarium was a bookcase
a collection of books; in modern French it means a bookshop, while a library is a bibliothèque
Chaucer uses 'librarie' in the 1370s; the British Museum, founded in 1753, held what became the British Library

current_meaning: a building or room containing books for people to read or borrow
